subject: Performance: PrismHealth VPC — degraded QPS and elevated 5xxs (exec bridge requested)
body:
--- Message 1/7 (2026-01-12T09:17:00-08:00) ---
From: Alex Romero <alex.romero@prismhealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@prismhealth.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: High p95 latency and 5xx spike in PrismHealth VPC - impact to claims API

Hi Grace,

We're seeing a sustained increase in p95 latency from ~420ms to ~1.9s across our claims inference route and a corresponding spike in 5xx errors starting ~08:45 PST. This is hitting our patient-facing workflows; throughput (qps) has dropped ~30% as requests are being retried. Our platform team flagged this to Priya and said execs want visibility.

Can Redwood confirm if anything changed on your side for our VPC cluster (model variant, kernel updates, autoscale)? We've attached a Grafana snapshot and a small log bundle. Please prioritize — we have a town hall at 3pm PT and need remediation ETA.

Attachments: prism_grafana_snapshot_01.png (png), prism_inference_logs_20260112.tar.gz (log bundle)

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Romero
Director, Platform Engineering
PrismHealth

--- Message 2/7 (2026-01-12T09:32:00-08:00) ---
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Romero <alex.romero@prismhealth.com>
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.ai, michael.grant@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High p95 latency and 5xx spike in PrismHealth VPC - impact to claims API

Alex — thank you for the heads up and attaching the snapshot. I'm escalating immediately to our on-call infra lead (Michael) and SE (Dev).

Short ask so we can triage quickly:
- Can you confirm the model id and version pinned on your VPC instance? (we've seen one customer switch to a longer-context variant accidentally)
- Is the spike isolated to the claims route? Any recent traffic pattern changes (larger batches, increased max_tokens)?
- If possible, please enable read-only link to the Grafana dashboard for our ops account.

We'll join your 3pm town hall if helpful — if execs want an interim bridge, we can host.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai

--- Message 3/7 (2026-01-12T10:06:00-08:00) ---
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Alex Romero <alex.romero@prismhealth.com>
Cc: michael.grant@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 10:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High p95 latency and 5xx spike in PrismHealth VPC - impact to claims API

Alex — I'm Dev (SE on-call). Reviewing logs now. Quick triage notes:
- From the logs you sent, I see elevated kv-cache misses and a backlog of requests queued on the dedicated pool workers (queue depth up ~3x).
- No evidence of a model variant switch in the first pass; version matches the pinned 1.4.2.
- I can see many requests with longer prompt prefixes; median input length has increased ~2.6x.

Immediate mitigations we can try (low risk):
1) Temporarily scale the dedicated pool by +30% capacity (short-term burst) — will require confirmation to use burst quota.
2) Enable prefix caching on the route (if not already enabled) to cut repeated context work.
3) Configure a short-lived routing fallback to the compatible quantized variant (v1.4.2-q8) for low-priority traffic to reduce pressure.

Please grant me read access to the Grafana link so I can correlate node-level metrics. If you want us to start the burst scale, say "go" and we'll queue the action.

Attachments referenced: support_escalation_form.pdf

—Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai

--- Message 6/7 (2026-01-12T16:10:00-08:00) ---
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 16:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: High p95 latency and 5xx spike in PrismHealth VPC - impact to claims API

Internal diagnostic summary (initial):
- Symptom: sustained p95 increase to ~1.9s; 5xx spike concentrated on two inference nodes in the private cluster.
- Likely proximate causes: higher median input size leading to longer per-request kernel execution; KV cache thrashing due to slightly different prompt prefixes; one node showing elevated GPU context switches (suspect memory pressure from background scheduled batch jobs).

Immediate actions (now — 30m):
- Action A (Dev): Enable routing fallback v1.4.2-q8 for low-priority traffic — expected p95 improvement ~25% for those requests.
- Action B (Ops): Burst scale dedicated pool +30% capacity (use customer's burst quota) — requires manual confirm from Alex (they gave permission in thread).
- Action C (Michael): Quarantine the two suspect nodes for detailed logs and redirect their traffic across the pool.

Medium-term tuning (24–72h):
- Audit prompt prefix patterns with Prism to identify repeated context that can be cached. (Owner: SE team)
- Apply conservative kernel scheduling tweak to reduce context switching on the nodes (Owner: Infra).
- Add per-route cache metrics to Prism's dashboard and increase retention for the critical 48h window.

Risks & rollbacks: fallback variant changes are reversible instantly, burst scaling may change billing; quarantining nodes will be lossless with live traffic redistribution.

I'll be on the 15:00 PT exec bridge unless leadership requests otherwise.

—Michael
Michael Grant
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.ai
[Attachment: support_escalation_form.pdf]

--- Message 7/7 (2026-01-13T17:42:00-08:00) ---
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Romero <alex.romero@prismhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Priya Kapoor <priya.kapoor@prismhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 17:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: High p95 latency and 5xx spike in PrismHealth VPC - impact to claims API

Alex / Priya — thank you for the bridge yesterday and for the fast collaboration. Quick status and next steps:

- What we did:
  * Burst scaled the dedicated pool (+30%) during the spike window.
  * Enabled v1.4.2-q8 routing fallback for low-priority requests (deployed at 10:25 PT).
  * Quarantined two suspect nodes and redistributed traffic — those nodes are under deeper post-mortem analysis.

- Impact now:
  * p95 reduced from ~1.9s to ~580–720ms across peak windows.
  * 5xx rate decreased from ~1.8% to 0.12% (still above target 0.1% but trending down).

- Next steps / commitments:
  1) SE + Prism team to run a prefix audit today to identify cacheable patterns (Owner: Dev / Alex) — ETA EOD 2026-01-13.
  2) Infra to ship a conservative kernel scheduling tweak and a targeted GC window for 48h retention (Owner: Michael) — ETA 2026-01-14 11:00 PT.
  3) Post-mortem with root cause analysis and tuning plan delivered by EOD 2026-01-14.

I've attached the runbook and the logs we gathered for your records. We also offered a usage credit to Prism for the period of degraded service; Laura will follow up on commercial remediation.

Attachments: prism_runbook_v1.docx (runbook)

If you'd like any additional detail before the post-mortem, say the word and we'll prioritize.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
